title: B2B software rep
tagline: Learn to navigate budget gates, prove ROI, and displace incumbents with skeptical finance leaders.
you_are: an enterprise account executive selling a finance-automation platform
setting: Conversations happen over scheduled video calls and in C-suite offices after a champion has secured a first meeting.

scenarios.label: First discovery call
scenarios.desc: A 30-minute video call to uncover pain and quantify the cost of inaction.
scenarios.setup: You are on a scheduled Zoom with a CFO who agreed to 30 minutes after your champion pushed internally. They open with: ‘I gave you half an hour because my controller insisted. Make it count.’
scenarios.objective: Secure a follow-up working session with the controller and IT lead.
scenarios.place: Video call from your home office
scenarios.moment: Tuesday 10:00 am, clean background, notebook ready

scenarios.label: ROI review meeting
scenarios.desc: A deep-dive session where the CFO stress-tests your business case against incumbent costs.
scenarios.setup: You sit across a conference table with the CFO and their controller. The CFO slides your model across the table and says: ‘Your NPV assumes 40 percent faster close. Show me the driver that isn’t hope.’
scenarios.skills: Financial modelling defence and competitive displacement
scenarios.objective: Get the CFO to sign off on a paid pilot scope and timeline.
scenarios.moment: Thursday 3:15 pm, late winter light through blinds

scenarios.label: Contract negotiation
scenarios.desc: Final round where the CFO presses on price, terms, and exit clauses before board sign-off.
scenarios.setup: You are back on video with the CFO alone. They lean in and say: ‘I like the pilot results. Now give me a three-year deal with a 90-day opt-out and 15 percent off list, or I walk to the board with the status quo.’
scenarios.objective: Close a multi-year agreement that protects margin and satisfies procurement.
scenarios.place: Video call from your home office

buyers.angle: Focuses on ROI before any discussion.
Wants to see concrete cost savings.
Clings to existing system despite new options.

objections: Our current budget is frozen for new software purchases
I need to see measurable ROI within six months
We already have a financial analytics tool, why change now
Implementation costs are too high for our scale
Can you guarantee data security in our regulatory environment
We cannot risk downtime during fiscal quarter end
Show me exactly how this reduces our expenses
Our board will reject any expense without clear cost justification

rubric.label: Pain quantification
rubric.what: Translate vague finance frustrations into hard numbers the CFO owns.

rubric.label: ROI modelling
rubric.what: Build and defend a business case that survives controller scrutiny.

rubric.label: Incumbent displacement
rubric.what: Articulate switching gains that outweigh migration cost and risk.

rubric.label: Stakeholder mapping
rubric.what: Identify and mobilise the controller, IT, and procurement allies.

rubric.label: Commercial negotiation
rubric.what: Trade concessions for commitment without eroding margin or compliance.

rubric.label: Contract compliance
rubric.what: Structure terms that pass legal, security, and audit review on first pass.

pitfalls: Promising implementation dates before technical validation.
Accepting opt-out clauses that void revenue recognition.
Sharing unredacted customer data in reference calls.
line: B2B software sales to skeptical CFOs

research.text: Common objections from skeptical CFOs in B2B software sales include concerns about cost and budget constraints. To address these, sellers suggest focusing on the outcomes that would make the investment worthwhile, helping buyers see the cost in the context of growth or efficiency. Skepticism about effectiveness can be countered by empathizing with the prospect's position, introducing the decision-maker to the product's benefits, and developing content that explores the solution's value. If a prospect already has a similar tool, emphasizing unique benefits, superior features, and potential cost savings or performance improvements can help. Additionally, generative AI tools like Microsoft's Copilot chatbot for finance workers are being introduced to address CFOs' concerns about implementation and maintenance.
